title: I Took the Office Badge Tailgating Report to the VP in the Vest

parts.text: I badged the lobby turnstile at 8:03 a.m. and felt a hand on the bar behind me. VP Chen in a visitor vest, which is what vendors wear, smiled like we were in on it. Security's poster said one badge, one body. I was thirty-two, IT ops, holding a coffee I did not want to spill on a VP. Chen said he had left his badge in the Tesla. I let the bar finish its cycle without him and pointed at the poster. He laughed and hopped the next bar when an intern scanned. The intern looked sick. I logged a tailgate with time, vest color, and the intern's name as witness. At 8:09 security's Slack asked who in a visitor vest just hopped turnstile two.
parts.cliffhanger_hint: Security Slack is asking while Chen is already in the elevator in a vendor vest.

social.video_title: The VP hopscotched the turnstile in a visitor vest — Part 1/2
social.description: One badge one body, Tesla story, intern witness. Slack woke up. Would you have let the bar close?

parts.text: Chen returned to the desk for a temporary badge that beeped every door like a confession. The intern was not written up. I was asked if I wanted to drop the log. I did not. Training assigned a two-minute video to all VPs titled Tailgating Is Not Leadership. Chen parks farther now and walks. The Tesla still exists. The vest went back to vendors. Turnstiles prefer numbers. I drink the coffee on the other side.

social.video_title: Temporary badges beep like confessions — Part 2/2
social.description: Intern safe, VP video, walking from the far lot. Was a Tesla a badge?
